LESSON: READING SYLLABLES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Reading syllables
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading syllables, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: How do we form syllables? 2.Where can we read letters of the alphabet?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading syllables together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: interacting with digital technology as learner listens to and observes recorded syllables from a digital

device.

● Learning to learn: as learner chants letters of the alphabet appropriately in groups, pairs and as individuals.

Values:
● Respect: patience as learner takes turn to chant and listen to others chant letters of the alphabet and read syllables.

● Unity: cooperation as learner works collaboratively with others as a team.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Social cohesion as learner harmoniously works with others to achieve common targets (reading letters and syllables).

Link to other Activity Areas:

Learner relates reading letter sounds (A-Z) in Language Activities with reading numbers 1,2,3,...26 in Mathematic

Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources: Adapted course book, signed audio visual clips, books, Flash cards, charts(manual

alphabet ), pictures, digital devices
